form.current-chamber: IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES

action.action-desc: Mr. Markey (for himself, Mr. Booker, Mr. Marshall, and Mr. Braun) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions

form.official-title: To increase access to medication for opioid overdose reversal, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Naloxone Affordability Act of 2023.

subsection.text: Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Comptroller General of the United States shall conduct a study on actions that may be taken to protect access to naloxone for individuals seeking to purchase naloxone. Such study shall address—

paragraph.text: coverage of naloxone (in any available form) as an over-the-counter product—

subparagraph.text: under a group health plan or group or individual health insurance coverage (as such terms are defined in section 2791 of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 300gg–91)); and

for individuals entitled to benefits under part A or enrolled under part B of title XVIII of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1395 et seq.) or receiving medical assistance under a State plan under title XIX of such Act (42 U.S.C. 1396 et seq.) (or a waiver of such plan); and

paragraph.text: the out-of-pocket cost to consumers purchasing naloxone under any such plan or coverage.

subsection.text: Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Comptroller General of the United States shall submit to Congress a report that contains the findings of the study conducted under subsection (a).
